newsitem.title: ALBANIA: EU urges Albania avoid force against rebels.
newsitem.headline: EU urges Albania avoid force against rebels.

text.p: The European Union urged Albanian President Sali Berisha on Friday to postpone or avoid altogether a resumption of military activity against armed rebels controlling parts of the south of the country.

"I urged the president to postpone as long as possible or refrain from violence," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo told a news conference after talks with Berisha. "I repeatedly said: 'Make it possible for the European Union to help Albania'."

Van Mierlo's one-day visit, under the auspices of the Dutch six-month presidency of the EU, was part of intensifying international efforts to end more than a month of violence, initially sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes. At least 25 people have died in the past week.
A Council of Europe delegation visited Tirana this week and former Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky was expected to arrive in the next few days.
Van Mierlo told Berisha the EU favoured fresh elections and a new constitution and said the president was considering such an approach.
He said it was up to Albanians to decide whether they wanted change through a new broader-based government or initially through an interim administration.
He said the EU could provide technical and humanitarian assistance but a bailout of Albanians, beggared by the demise of the pyramid schemes, was impossible.

"It is not this very day that Albania can come to the solutions we hope for," he said. "I had a very frank discussion on this approach and I think that in due course the president will make up his mind on what he has to do."

Parliament, dominated by Berisha's Democratic Party, proclaimed a state of emergency last weekend. A two-day suspension of the army's advance on insurgents in the south, approved by Berisha and Albania's major political parties, is in effect until early on Sunday.
But rebels rejected an offer of an amnesty and said they would lay down their weapons only when Berisha, re-elected this week by parliament to a new five-year term, stepped down.

Van Mierlo acknowledged that opposition parties had limited influence but urged them to do their utmost to halt violence and to take up the handful of seats in parliament they won in last May's disputed election.

The head of the Council of Europe delegation, Dutch parliamentarian Rene Van den Linden, earlier welcomed the two-day halt to military activity and called on all political parties to condemn violence.
